newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia deals fresh blow to BP oil operations.
newsitem.headline: Colombia deals fresh blow to BP oil operations.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc suffered a setback to its Colombian oil operations Friday when the Mines and Energy Ministry reversed an earlier decision that would have boosted the short-term profitability of a field the company operates in the east of the country.
The British multinational and the Colombian government are involved in a protracted wrangle over the terms of the contract to exploit the giant Piedemonte block in the eastern plains region.

Under the current so-called sliding scale formula, the state-run oil company Ecopetrol takes an increasing slice of the profits as output increases - a deal which BP long complained was not sufficiently profitable.

Last month, Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar ruled that natural gas output would be used as the benchmark by which the profit split would be determined instead of crude. In practical terms this meant BP would retain a larger share of the profits for a longer time.
But in the face of a nationalistic outcry from legislators and union leaders that BP, Colombia's single largest foreign investor, was pressuring the nation, Villamizar reversed his decision Friday.
"I have revoked that decision," the minister told reporters, adding that the issue would be referred back to Ecopetrol's board of directors for further consideration.

For its part BP said it would not start commercial production in Piedemonte until the wrangle was sorted out, saying that it and the nation would lose $5 million for every week that the dispute lasted.
"We have put back the start of commercial production, which we had been set to begin in the next few weeks," a spokesman told Reuters.

BP has invested about $2.1 billion in developing three hydrocarbon formations in Piedemonte - equivalent to just 15 percent of the total field which is still largely unexplored. Those three formations alone are estimated to contain between 500 million and 1 billion barrels of condensates.
